title: SASSA SRD R370 Grant 2026: Eligibility, Payment Dates & How to Apply
description: Comprehensive breakdown of the SASSA SRD R370 grant for 2026. The grant amount is {{srd_grant_amount}}/month. Who qualifies, required documents, how to apply, the latest confirmed 2026 payment dates, what 'Approved' means, and what to do if your application is declined.
author: Lucky Cungwa

sections.title: What is the SRD R370 Grant?
sections.content: The Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant, commonly known as the SASSA SRD R370 grant, is a temporary monthly payment from the South African government to unemployed adults who are not receiving any other form of social assistance. Originally introduced as a R350 grant during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, it was increased to {{srd_grant_amount}} in April 2024. The old R350 name still refers to this same grant, and it has become a vital lifeline for millions of South Africans. As of 2026, the grant continues to be a vital lifeline, with cover basic needs like food, transport, and essentials. The grant is paid in the last week of each month.

sections.title: Eligibility — Who Qualifies for the SRD R370?
sections.content:
To qualify for the SASSA SRD R370 grant in 2026, you must meet all the following requirements:
  • South African citizenship or legal residency: You must be a South African citizen, permanent resident, refugee, asylum seeker, or special permit holder.
  • Age: You must be between {{srd_age_range_min}} and {{srd_age_range_max}} years old. If you are 60 or older, you qualify for the Older Persons Grant instead.
  • Income threshold: Your monthly income must be below {{srd_income_limit}}. SASSA checks your bank accounts across all major South African banks to verify this.
  • No other grant: You must not be receiving any other social grant, UIF payments, or NSFAS funding.
  • Not in institutional care: You must not be living in a state-funded institution.

sections.title: Income Limits Explained
sections.content:
The {{srd_income_limit}} income threshold is strictly enforced. SASSA has agreements with all major South African banks (Absa, FNB, Standard Bank, Capitec, Nedbank, and others) to monitor total monthly deposits into accounts linked to your ID number. This includes:
  • Salary or wages from any form of employment
  • Money received from family or friends
  • Income from informal trading or small business
  • Interest earned on savings
  • Any other regular or irregular deposits
If the total deposits in any month exceed {{srd_income_limit}}, your application for that month will be declined.

sections.title: Required Documents
sections.content:
You need the following to apply for the SRD {{srd_grant_amount}} grant:
  • South African ID document — green ID book, smart ID card, or temporary ID certificate
  • Valid South African mobile number — registered in your name (RICA'd)
  • Proof of banking details — bank statement or a screenshot of your banking app showing account holder name and account number
  • Proof of residence (only if requested during verification)
  • Refugee or asylum seeker permit — if applicable

steps.title: Visit the Official SRD Portal
steps.content: Go to srd.sassa.gov.za on your phone or computer. This is the only official application portal. Avoid third-party websites that charge fees.

steps.title: Enter Your ID Number
steps.content: Type your full 13-digit South African ID number. Double-check for typos — a single wrong digit will cause identity verification to fail.

steps.title: Enter Your Mobile Number
steps.content: Use the mobile number that is registered in your name. You will receive SMS updates about your application status.

steps.title: Provide Banking Details
steps.content: Enter your bank account details where you want the grant paid. You can use any South African bank account, including Capitec, FNB, Absa, Standard Bank, Nedbank, TymeBank, or Postbank.

steps.title: Submit and Wait for Confirmation
steps.content: After submitting, you will receive an SMS confirmation. Your application will be processed, and you can check your status on the same portal.

sections.title: Payment Dates for 2026
sections.content: The SRD {{srd_grant_amount}} grant does not have a fixed payment date like permanent grants. Instead, payments are processed in batches during the last week of each month. For example, SASSA confirmed the October 2026 SRD {{srd_grant_amount}} payment dates as Thursday 22 and Friday 23 October 2026. Beneficiaries are paid in a batch on either date according to their personal 'Pay Day' on the SRD portal, not on both dates. The SRD grant has been extended until 31 March 2027. Check the official SRD portal for your personal 'Pay Day' date. The fourth payment day for grants under review is not yet confirmed. Once your status shows a 'Pay Day' date, it is confirmed for you. After your 'Pay Day' date, it can take up to 48 business hours for the money to reflect in your account. You do not need to withdraw everything on the first day - your money is safe in your account.

sections.title: October 2026: Confirmed Payment Dates
sections.content: SASSA confirmed the October 2026 payment dates for the permanent grants: Older Persons Grant on Friday, 2 October, Disability Grant on Monday, 5 October, and Children's Grants on Tuesday, 6 October - these dates have now passed. SASSA also confirmed the October {{srd_grant_amount}} SRD payment dates as Thursday 22 and Friday 23 October 2026; you are paid on one of those two dates according to your personal 'Pay Day' on the SRD portal, not on both. The fourth payment day for grants under review is not yet confirmed. Read the full October 2026 schedule and the payment calendar for the latest confirmed dates, and the November 2026 schedule for the next cycle.

sections.title: What Does 'Approved' Mean for the SRD Grant?
sections.content: When your status shows 'Approved', it means SASSA has confirmed you qualify for the {{srd_grant_amount}} SRD grant for that month and your payment is being processed. It does not mean the money is already in your bank account. After approval, your status will later show a 'Pay Day' date - this is when the payment batch is released. The money can then take up to 48 business hours to reflect in your account. See our full explanation of what Approved means.

sections.title: Approved But No Pay Day - What Now?
sections.content: Early in the month it is normal for your status to show 'Approved' without a 'Pay Day' date yet. SRD statuses are refreshed around the middle of each month, and the payment date appears once the batch for that month is confirmed. Do not contact SASSA about it yet - wait until after the middle of the month and check again. If you are approved but your payment date passes without the money arriving, read our guide on Approved but no pay day and the missing grant payment guide before calling 0800 60 10 11.

sections.title: Why Was I Approved One Month, Declined the Next?
sections.content: The SRD grant is reassessed every single month. Approval in one month does not guarantee approval in the next, because your circumstances are re-checked against your bank accounts, UIF, SARS, NSFAS and Home Affairs records each cycle. A bank deposit that pushed your total over {{srd_income_limit}}, a UIF payment received, an NSFAS record still showing as active, or a Home Affairs data update can each trigger a decline for the new month. A decline for one month does not cancel your application for the following month, and it does not mean you lost the grant permanently. Check the decline reason on the portal and appeal within 90 days if it is wrong. See our SRD reapplication and renewal guide and the appeal guide.

sections.title: What If My SRD Grant Was Cancelled?
sections.content: If your SRD status shows your grant was cancelled, do not panic. Cancellation can happen if you did not collect for three consecutive months, if you no longer meet the eligibility criteria, or if SASSA flagged your application during verification. A cancelled grant is not a permanent ban - you can reapply at any time on the official SRD portal with your 13-digit ID number. Your reapplication is assessed on the same monthly cycle as new applications. If a specific month was declined, you can appeal that month within 90 days. A cancellation with no declined month is handled by reapplying, not by an appeal. See our renewal guide for the full steps.

sections.title: Payment Problems - What to Do Step by Step

steps.title: Check Your Status First
steps.content: Log in to the official SRD portal (srd.sassa.gov.za) with your 13-digit ID number and check your current status. If it shows 'Referred', 'Under Review' or 'Declined', that explains the missing payment.

steps.title: Wait for Your 'Pay Day' Date
steps.content: If your status shows 'Approved', look for the 'Pay Day' date. The payment batch may not have been released yet, or the money can take up to 48 business hours to reflect in your bank account after the pay day.

steps.title: Confirm Your Banking Details
steps.content: Make sure the bank account on your application is correct and active. If your banking details are pending, see our bank details fix guide (/guides/bank-details-pending-fix).

steps.title: Wait for the SMS If Collecting at Retail
steps.content: If you collect at Pick n Pay, Boxer, Shoprite, Checkers or USave, do not go to the store until you receive the official payment SMS containing your collection code.

steps.title: Follow the Missing Payment Guide
steps.content: If the money still has not arrived, follow the missing grant payment guide (/guides/missing-grant-payment-guide) step by step, then contact the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11.

faqs.q: What is the confirmed SRD payment date for October 2026?
faqs.a: SASSA confirmed the October 2026 SRD payment dates as Thursday 22 and Friday 23 October 2026. The SRD is paid in batches, so you are paid on one of those two dates according to your own 'Pay Day' on the official SRD portal, not on both dates. The fourth payment day for grants under review is not yet confirmed.

faqs.q: My status shows 'Approved' but I have no 'Pay Day' date. What does this mean?
faqs.a: This is normal early in the month. SRD statuses are refreshed around the middle of each month, and the payment date appears once the batch is confirmed. Wait and check your status again after the middle of the month. Read more at /status/approved.

faqs.q: I was approved last month but declined this month. Why?
faqs.a: The SRD grant is reassessed fresh every month. Changes in your bank deposits, UIF, SARS, NSFAS or Home Affairs records can trigger a decline even if nothing felt different to you. A decline for one month does not cancel your application for the next month. Check the decline reason and appeal within 90 days.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not collect my grant?
faqs.a: If you do not collect your grant for three consecutive months, your application may be suspended. You will need to reapply by visiting srd.sassa.gov.za and submitting a fresh application. Your banking details are usually kept, but you should verify your details after reapplying.

faqs.q: Can someone collect my grant on my behalf?
faqs.a: Yes, but only if you have registered them as an authorized proxy with SASSA. The proxy must present their ID and a letter of authorization.

sections.title: Payment Methods
sections.content:
You can receive your SRD grant through:
  • Bank transfer — directly into your South African bank account
  • Postbank — collect at any Postbank branch or Post Office
  • Retail collection — collect at Pick n Pay, Boxer, Shoprite, Checkers, or USave using the SMS code sent to your phone
To collect at a retail store, you must receive the official payment SMS containing your collection code. Do not go to the store until you have received this SMS.

sections.title: How to Reapply for the SRD Grant
sections.content: Reapplying is only needed in specific situations: do not reapply just because you were declined for a month. A decline usually means a monthly reassessment flagged something - the correct step is to check the decline reason and lodge a free appeal on the ITSAA portal within 90 days. See our appeal guide for the steps. You should only reapply when your status actually asks you to, such as a 'Reapplication Pending' or 'reapplication_required' status after your application lapsed or failed to add approval within the allowed time. Reapplying a declined application can reset your cycle and delay your next payment. When reapplication is required, it is free: go to srd.sassa.gov.za and submit a new application with your 13-digit ID number. The official WhatsApp and Moya App are not confirmed reapplication channels - use the portal. After reapplying, check your status after the 15th of the month; reapplications are assessed on the same monthly cycle as new applications. Our dedicated SRD reapplication guide explains the difference between a decline and a required reapplication step by step.

faqs.q: Can I apply if I am a student?
faqs.a: Yes, you can apply if you are a student, as long as you are not receiving NSFAS funding. However, students who are registered with NSFAS may be declined automatically.

faqs.q: Can I receive SRD if I have a part-time job?
faqs.a: Yes, but only if your total monthly income is below {{srd_income_limit}}. If your part-time income exceeds this threshold, you will not qualify for that month.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not collect my grant?
faqs.a: If you do not collect your grant for three consecutive months, your application may be suspended. You will need to reapply by visiting srd.sassa.gov.za and submitting a fresh application. Your banking details are usually kept, but you should verify your details after reapplying.

faqs.q: How do I reapply for the SRD grant?
faqs.a: To reapply, go to the official SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za and submit a new application with your 13-digit ID number. You can also reapply via the SASSA WhatsApp line (082 601 0111) or the Moya App. Reapplication is free and does not require visiting a SASSA office.

faqs.q: Can someone collect my grant on my behalf?
faqs.a: Yes, but only if you have registered them as an authorized proxy with SASSA. The proxy must present their ID and a letter of authorization.

Yes. The 2026 National Budget (announced 19 February 2026) confirmed funding for the SRD R370 grant through 31 March 2027, and SASSA is still processing payments every month. The grant amount stays at {{srd_grant_amount}} for now. Any decision on what happens after March 2027 will be announced by the Minister of Finance and the Department of Social Development - watch our budget update for the latest (/updates/update-2026-014).
